meta.title: ASITECH OPS — Open source multi-server deployment and management
meta.description: Open source platform (Apache 2.0) to deploy, manage and monitor your applications across all your Linux servers from a single dashboard. Maintained by ASITECH SOLUTION.
meta.ogAlt: ASITECH OPS — deploy and manage your applications on all your Linux servers

hero.title: Deploy and manage your applications on all your Linux servers, from a single dashboard.
hero.subtitle: ASITECH OPS is an open source deployment and infrastructure management platform: a central Control Plane, lightweight agents on your servers, and Docker at its core. Released under the Apache 2.0 license by ASITECH SOLUTION.
hero.illustrationCaption: Illustration of the planned interface — not a screenshot. Real screenshots will be published with the first releases.

features.title: Everything you need to run your applications
features.subtitle: The modules planned for ASITECH OPS. Their availability is tracked in the roadmap.

multiServer.title: Multi-server
multiServer.text: Operate one VPS or a whole fleet of Linux servers from the same dashboard.

git.title: Git deployments
git.text: Deploy a branch from a Git repository, with build commands and environment variables.

docker.title: Docker & Compose
docker.text: Image builds with BuildKit and Docker Compose stack deployments.

logs.title: Real-time logs
logs.text: Follow build and container logs live, without opening an SSH session.

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.text: CPU, memory, disk, network and application health, with history.

domains.title: Domains & SSL

rollback.title: Rollback

teams.title: Teams & permissions
teams.text: Organizations, roles, invitations and an audit log for every sensitive action.

how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: Three steps, from your first VPS to your first deployment.

steps.title: Install the Control Plane
steps.text: A verified installer (SHA-256 checksum) deploys the dashboard, API, PostgreSQL and Redis with Docker Compose, without touching the services you already run.

steps.title: Connect servers with the agent
steps.text: Install the agent on each Linux server. It registers with a unique, revocable identity and opens an encrypted outbound connection.

steps.title: Deploy from Git
steps.text: Pick a repository and a branch: ASITECH OPS builds the image, deploys it, checks its health and keeps the history so you can roll back.

architecture.title: An architecture designed for security
architecture.subtitle: A central Control Plane and remote agents. Agents connect to the Control Plane: no management port is opened on your servers.
architecture.diagramDesc: The central Control Plane receives outbound TLS connections initiated by the agent installed on each Linux server. Each agent drives Docker locally.
notes: Agents initiate the connection (WebSocket over TLS): no public management API on your servers.
Every task is validated, timestamped and time-limited; no arbitrary shell commands.
This public website is static and fully isolated from the platform.

security.title: Security, without vague promises
security.subtitle: Principles applied from the design stage. The full threat model is documented in the repository.

items.title: TLS everywhere
items.text: Encrypted traffic between agents, Control Plane and browser.

items.title: Revocable agent credentials
items.text: Each server has a unique identity that can be revoked at any time.

items.title: No arbitrary shell execution
items.text: The API only accepts defined, validated operations.

items.title: Audit log
items.text: Sensitive actions are recorded and cannot be modified.

items.title: Organization isolation
items.text: An organization can never access another organization's resources.

items.title: Docker socket risk documented
items.text: Docker socket access is root-equivalent: it is treated as such and tightly controlled.

install.title: Install
install.subtitle: On a supported Ubuntu server: download the installer, verify its SHA-256 checksum, then run it.
install.notLive: This distribution endpoint is not live yet: the VPS installer ships in Phase 5. Never run an unverified installation script in production.
install.requirements: Planned: Ubuntu LTS, 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, Docker Engine. Ports 80/443 already in use are detected: integration with your existing proxy is supported.

openSource.title: Open source, for real
openSource.subtitle: All the code — platform, agent, installer and this website — is published under the Apache 2.0 license. Contributions are welcome.
openSource.invite: Developers, DevOps engineers, writers, translators: every contribution counts.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.subtitle: The project moves phase by phase. A feature is only marked “done” when it actually works.

items.a: Yes. The code is open source under the Apache 2.0 license: you can use, modify and redistribute it, including commercially, as long as you follow the license.
The Control Plane and the agent target Linux servers, Ubuntu LTS with Docker Engine first. The exact list will be published with the installer.

items.q: Can I keep my existing Nginx?
items.a: Yes. The installer never disables an existing proxy: if ports 80/443 are taken, it offers integration with your proxy, dedicated ports, or installation on a dedicated VPS.
Not yet. The project is in early development; this website will clearly say when a stable release is available.

items.q: How do I report a vulnerability?
items.a: Privately, by e-mail to {securityEmail}, not in a public issue. The process is described in SECURITY.md.
